<!-- pr-reviewer: fd1a1c94b27d17076f1ad7d0a89e0fbbb454ae2b -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**


Read in full: the new modules, the guard and step hunks, the new test file, the decision file and the head of the fixture.

**What looks good**
- No panic path was found in the new code. `step_pole`/`step_edge3d` have no `unwrap`/`expect`/indexing. `knot_domain` returns `None` for non-finite or empty ranges. `settle` checks the replacement against the searched point, and a NaN distance fails the comparison, so the answer stays as truck found it.
- The #1546 guard is not weakened. The metered wrapper still counts evaluations and refuses by name. `settle` only post-processes a parameter-search answer, and it returns a replacement only when the surface there is the searched point (1e-6). Anything else keeps the old behaviour, still bounded by the meter. `step_guard.rs` changes only add the `settle` calls and a doc update. `import_step_guard` is unchanged.
- Nothing is silently replaced by a wrong surface. A replacement is taken only when it is the same point, otherwise the face keeps the existing refusal.
- Bounded work: no loop or allocation sized by file content was added. `prefer_3d` is a single pass over the edge and surface-curve tables.
- Tolerance and closure are pinned. The main test asserts bounds to 1e-9 and 0 open edges after welding (orientation-aware). It asserts volume short of the closed form by 0 ..= `CHORD_CAP` x curved area, and `coarse_mm == None`. The reversed-edge test pins the `same_sense = .F.` path. The 10 bent variants run under a 90 s limit and a 200k evaluation cap.
- Mutation checks are in the PR body, and each pin was seen RED.
- The fixture comes from the project's own kernel (solidcore step-export), not another product's files. The recipe is in the PR body. The `FILE_DESCRIPTION` says so.
- Provenance lines, a decision file, a `Changelog:` line and `Fixes #1548` are present. No process files, dependencies or snapshots are touched.

**Results merged with main**
- On the self-hosted runner: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/actions/runs/43522586793 (success; PR head merged with main ce814fe5): quick gate green (app suites, 60 s, 0 failed), clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings clean. Plus the author-reported results on the same head.
- Windows-only readings: none in the diff (no `cfg(windows)`).

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Questions / notes (not blocking)**
1. The bent-blend fuzz test asserts only finite facets or a refusal, not closure. The PR admits three variants import with the blend face dropped, an open mesh with no warning (filed as #1573, P1). That gap exists on main as well, and this PR neither adds nor widens it. It stays the priority follow-up, since the importer can still produce a silently open shell for a corrupt blend.
2. The maintainer's `sc_logo.step` repro on this branch is still owed, as the author notes. The readings come from a rebuild with a different writer.
3. `prefer_3d` switches every surface curve's master to the 3D curve for all STEP imports, not only blends. Existing STEP suites are green per the author. Any model whose 3D curve and pcurves disagree now follows the 3D curve. That is the standard-compliant choice, but it is a wider change than the title says.
4. Release-mode timing and the GUI import path were not exercised.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
